title: When is the sum of three numbers divisible by three?
description: Any three numbers are sorted by their remainders on division by three. The video tries all ten ways the remainders can fall, finds which add to a multiple of three, and states one rule.
teaching_notes: One idea: only the remainders on division by three decide whether the sum is divisible by three, so listing the cases for the remainders covers every number. Watch for students who test a few triples of numbers and state a rule without covering all the cases.

video_script.why: The student can add numbers by adding their remainders and regrouping, and now uses that to cover every case for three numbers on division by three.
video_script.substitution: Replace each number by its remainder on division by three, list every way three remainders can fall, and add them.
video_script.anchor: dots in groups of three, each number with zero, one or two dots loose, as in the book's pictures of remainders
video_script.payoff_line: The sum is divisible by three when the remainders are all the same or all different

final_answer.value: When the three numbers leave the same remainder on division by 3, or three different remainders
final_answer.spoken: when the three numbers leave the same remainder on division by three, or three different remainders

hold_back: all the same or all different
maths_rules: each number leaves remainder 0, 1 or 2 on division by 3
the sum is divisible by 3 when the three remainders add to 0, 3 or 6
video_script.design: Each number is groups of three with zero, one or two dots loose. The ten ways three loose counts can fall are listed in two sets, then three real triples check the rule.

Zero, zero, zero add to zero, and one, one, one add to three.
<bookmark mark='twos'/>Two, two, two add to six.
<bookmark mark='diff'/>Try three different remainders, and zero, one, two add to three.
<bookmark mark='tick'/>All four of these cases work.

narration: <bookmark mark='others'/>Step three, try the other six cases. Zero, zero, one add to one, and zero, zero, two add to two.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Zero, one, one add to two, and zero, two, two add to four.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>One, one, two add to four, and one, two, two add to five.
<bookmark mark='cross'/>None of these totals is zero, three or six.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check: 4 + 7 + 10 = 21 = 3 x 7; 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 = 3 x 4; 1 + 2 + 4 = 7, not divisible by 3

marks.ex1: four, seven and ten are split in threes, each with one over, and their sum twenty one is seven threes

narration: <bookmark mark='ex1'/>Step four, check with real numbers. Four, seven and ten each leave remainder one, and their sum is twenty one.
That is three times seven.
<bookmark mark='ex2'/>Three, four and five leave remainders zero, one and two, and their sum is twelve.
That is three times four.
<bookmark mark='ex3'/>One, two and four leave remainders one, two and one, and their sum is seven.
Seven is not divisible by three.
